store.name: OmniCompost
store.tagline: The digester and everything that keeps the loop running.

products.name: The Digester
products.alt2: Red wiggler worms in finished compost
products.blurb: The centerpiece — a stacked-tray vermicomposter in powder-coated steel and beechwood, sized for a household of four. Worms up top, compost tea drawn from a brass tap below.
products.desc: The centerpiece. A stacked-tray vermicomposter in powder-coated steel and beechwood, sized for a household of four. Worms work the upper trays; finished compost and tea draw from a brass tap below. Quiet, odorless when balanced, and built to sit in a kitchen rather than hide in a garage.
details: Sized for a household of four
Odorless when the bin is balanced

products.name: The Mini Digester
products.alt: The OmniCompost mini digester on a balcony
products.desc: The digester, sized down for a balcony or a galley kitchen. A two-tray vermicomposter in the same powder-coated steel and beechwood, with a footprint that fits a railing ledge or a corner by the door. It takes a smaller household's scraps — roughly half the daily volume — and works at an unhurried pace, so a single person or a couple never overfeeds it. Same brass tap, same quiet, same finished compost in a frame that asks for a fraction of the floor.
details: Sized for one or two — about half the daily volume

products.name: Red Wigglers
products.desc: Eisenia fetida — the red wiggler, the worm that does the work. One pound establishes the digester and roughly doubles its population across a season of steady feeding. Shipped live in moist bedding, ready for the top tray.
details: Doubles in a season under steady feeding

products.name: Worm Starter Kit
products.alt2: TEMP-COMP — hands settling plants into fresh soil (watermarked Unsplash+ comp; remove once seat confirmed)
products.desc: Everything the bin needs on day one — coir bedding, a mineral grit, and a feeding guide keyed to the first six weeks. Pairs with a pound of worms to bring a new digester up to temperature without guesswork.

products.name: Bedding Bricks ×3
products.desc: Three compressed coir bricks — each expands to roughly 8 liters in warm water. Bedding is the carbon half of the bin; refresh a handful whenever the trays read wet or the balance tips sour.

products.name: Harvest Trowel
products.alt2: Garden hand tools hung on a weathered wood door
products.desc: A narrow stainless trowel sized for tray work — deep enough to lift a finished layer, slim enough to leave the worms behind. Beechwood handle to match the digester.

products.name: Tea Watering Can
products.alt2: The watering can in use among garden flowers
products.desc: A two-liter can in glazed stoneware, filled straight from the digester's tap. The long spout reaches the base of a pot; the mark inside reads half-and-half, so the tea goes out at strength.

products.name: Seedling Pots ×6
products.alt2: Hands settling a seedling into dark soil
products.desc: Six terracotta pots, 7 cm across — sized for the seedlings the compost will raise. Unglazed, so the roots breathe and the soil dries evenly between waterings.

products.name: Tea Concentrate
products.desc: A bottled head-start for a young bin — a measured culture of the microbes finished compost carries. One capful seeds the first brew while the worms find their rhythm.

products.name: The Whole Loop
products.alt2: The loop's tools gathered in greenhouse light
products.desc: The digester and everything that keeps it running — worms, bedding, the starter kit, trowel, watering can, and a season of tea concentrate, gathered into one order. Saves $66 over buying the loop piece by piece.
